To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
axonal kainate receptors (KAR) promote presynaptic differentiation and increase the probability of evoked neurotransmitter release.

the calcium permeable kainate type of receptors (KAR), but not the calcium-imperable KARs, increase the probability of synaptic transmission in a presynaptic manner by promoting the differentiation of presynaptic terminals.
the presence of functional axonal KARs increases the number of functional synapses by promoting the formation of presynaptic release zones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of synaptic transmission and plastic changes during the development and maturation of the nervous system.
the role of axonal KARs in synaptic development and plasticity.
the role of Kainate type glutamate receptors (KA-Rs) during development and function in the nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the calcium-permeable variants of KARs, but not the calcium-imper-meable variants or the KARs of the GluK4/5 subtypes, promote presynaptic differentiation in a manner that increases the probability of evoked glutamate release.
KARs in presinaptic neurons regulate synaptic development and function by increasing the probability of glutamate exocytosis.
KARs in axons modulate presynaptic differentiation and thereby influence the probability of synaptic transmission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
axonal KARs regulate presynaptic differentiation, and thereby modulate the efficacy of efferent connectivity.
KARs are important for the development of presynaptic terminals.
KARs in axons modulate the strength of efferent connectivity via regulation of presynaptic release site differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
axonal KARs can influence the development of presynaptic terminals and the efficacy of glutamatergic transmission by regulating the density of active zones and release probability.
the calcium permeable variants of axonal KARs are important for regulating synaptic density and efficacy by modulating presynaptic differentiation.
axonal KARs are important for regulating the density of functional synapses.
